pr_title: network: check lifetime of address and route before configure
pr_body:
Otherwise, we may configure a route that depends on the existence of an address or another route, and may fail when lifetime of one of them are already zero.

Hopefully fixes #28358.

issue_context.title: Bug: systemd-networkd does not properly connect to network after suspend
issue_context.body:
### systemd version the issue has been seen with

systemd 253 (253.5-2-arch)

### Used distribution

ArchLinux

### Linux kernel version used

6.1.38-1-lts

### CPU architectures issue was seen on

x86_64

### Component

systemd-networkd

### Expected behaviour you didn't see

Network interfaces should be configured as described in the .network files on the system and like they are after a fresh system boot.
Specifically:
* 1 statically configured private IPv4 address
* 2 dynamically configured IPv6 addresses (via SLAAC): one with the default euid64 token, one with a static token.
* 1 statically configured ULA-only-IPv6  address

### Unexpected behaviour you saw

Randomly missing interface or route configurations.
Seen miss-configurations:

* (Private) IPv4, ULA based IPv6 and Link Local IPv6 correctly set, GUA based IPv6 addresses missing
* IPv4 correctly set, no IPv6 connectivity whatsoever
* No network connectivity at all (this is a headless system without management interfaces, so diagnosing this case is pretty much impossible and requires a hardware reboot)
* ULA based IPv6 and LLIPv6 correctly set, no GUA based IPv6 and missing gateway for IPv4 and IPv6, so only local connectivity

### Steps to reproduce the problem

### Setup
The system is a headless, local Home-Server/NAS in a consumer grade dual-stack private network.
The Router advertises the dynamic global IPv6 prefix and a custom static ULA prefix.
DHCP and DHCPv6 are both enabled and used to distribute gateway and DNS settings.
Docker is setup on the host but in the log output below messages related to the many veth interfaces are removed. (tell me if they are relevant)
Wake-On-Lan is enabled in the UEFI.

### Configuration files
/etc/systemd/network/50-wired.link
```
[Match]
MACAddress=<REDACTED MAC>

[Link]
NamePolicy=keep kernel database onboard slot path
AlternativeNamesPolicy=database onboard slot path
MACAddressPolicy=persistent
WakeOnLan=magic
```

Please note that the Static address configurations are an attempt to work around this bug and have no impact in it at all.

/etc/systemd/network/20-wired.network
```
[Match]
Name=enp1s0

[Network]
Address=192.168.0.4/24
Gateway=192.168.0.1
DNS=192.168.0.1
DNS=<READACTED IPv6 of DNS>
IPv6PrivacyExtensions=yes
Address=<REDACTED ULA Prefix+STATIC1>/64
Address=<REDACTED ULA Prefix+STATIC_TOKEN>/64
Address=<REDACTED ULA Prefix+EUI64>/64
IPv6AcceptRA=1
DHCP=yes

[IPv6AcceptRA]
Token=eui64
Token=static:::<REDACTED STATIC_TOKEN>
UseRoutePrefix=true
UseGateway=yes

[DHCPv4]
UseDNS=yes
UseNTP=yes
UseGateway=yes

[DHCPv6]
UseDNS=yes
UseNTP=yes

[Route]
Gateway=<READACTED LLIPv6 of Gateway>
```
### How to reproduce
1. login via ssh
2. put the system to sleep with:
```
systemctl suspend && logout
```
3. wait some time (usually overnight)
4. send a magic packet to wakeup the system with:
```wol <MAC_ADDRESS>```
5. wait a few seconds
6. try to ssh into the system again
7. If it doesn't work, try some of the other addresses (ULA, GUA, LLv6, v4, v6) - (otherwise the bug did not occur this time)
8.1 If Unable to connect => use hardware button to reboot - (bug occurred! system works perfectly fine if you could connect to it)
8.2 If able to connect => verify with `ip addr` that not all IP-addresses have been configured. `ping` and DNS queries might fail because of missing routes, "unreachable networks" or unreachable DNS resolvers.
9. restarting the systemd-networkd service fixes the issue

```
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# try to reconfigure a link that is not currently configured
# Copyright 2023 Tj <linux@iam.tj>
# Licensed on the terms of the GNU General Public Licence version 3.
# workaround for suspend/resume when link fails
#  see: https://github.com/systemd/systemd/issues/28358
#  "systemd-networkd does not properly connect to network after suspend"
#
# To install and enable for interface LINK:
# copy this script to /usr/local/bin/wol_wakeup_recover
#
#  chmod +x /usr/local/bin/wol_wakeup_recover
#  /usr/local/bin/wol_wakeup_recover LINK install
#
# this creates a template unit and then enables the @LINK service.
# On resume the unit executes this script. The script simply loops
# a few times waiting for LINK to report 'configured'
# Log entries are written to aid debugging and testing.
#
# To disable and uninstall the per-link service:
#
#  /usr/local/bin/wol_wakeup_recover LINK uninstall
#
# To remove the template service unit:
#
# sudo rm /etc/systemd/system/wol_wakeup_recover@.servicve
#
# The script will warn if the installed systemd-networkd version is v253 or later
# because that version includes the upstream fix for the issue.

# no link given
[[ -z "$1" ]] && exit 1
# link does not exist
# output is menat to be captured by the journal to aid any debugging
networkctl list "$1" || exit 1
# link is not managed
networkctl list "$1" | grep -q unmanaged && exit 0

# check whether this workaround is still required
networkd_version="$(/usr/lib/systemd/systemd-networkd --version | grep '^systemd' | cut -d\  -f 2)"
networkd_version_fixed="253"

# default service name is this script's basename 
service="${service:-${0##*/}}"
link="$1"

service_install() {
	# call this script from a system service
	local template
	template="/etc/systemd/system/${service}@.service"

	if [[ $networkd_version -ge $networkd_version_fixed ]]; then
		printf "%s\n" "$service@$link: this workaround should no longer be required since systemd version $networkd_version_fixed"
	fi

	if ! [[ -f "$template" ]]; then
		printf "%s\n" "Creating service template $template"
		cat <<-EOF > "$template"
		[Unit]
		Description=Force network link reconfigure after suspend
		After=suspend.target
		Requires=suspend.target

		[Service]
		Type=oneshot
		ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/$service %i

		[Install]
		RequiredBy=suspend.target
		EOF

		systemctl daemon-reload
	fi

	systemctl enable "$service@$link.service"
	return $?
}


service_uninstall() {
	if systemctl status "$service@$link.service"; then
		systemctl disable --now "$service@$link.service"
	else
		printf "%s\n" "service does not exist"
		return 1
	fi
}

if [[ -n "$2" ]]; then
	if [[ "$2" = "install" ]]; then
		service_install
	elif [[ "$2" = "uninstall" ]]; then
		service_uninstall
	else
		printf "%s\n" "usage: $0 LINK [install | uninstall]"
	fi
fi

# retry several times
declare -i tries=6
declare -i count=$tries
while [[ $count -ne 0 ]] && ! networkctl list "$link" | grep -q configured ; do
  networkctl reconfigure "$link"
	(( count-- ))
	logger --id=$$ "reconfigure $link: try: $count"
	sleep 10
done

if [[ $networkd_version -ge $networkd_version_fixed ]]; then
	logger --id=$$ "$service@$link: this workaround should no longer be required since systemd version $networkd_version_fixed"
fi

result=0
if [[ $count -eq 0 ]]; then
	result=1
fi

exit $result
```
